stem: A child is referred for chronic loose stools, but serial measurements show weight, height, and head circumference all crossing down; which alternative explanation is most supported?

options.text: Increased loss from diarrhoea or malabsorption

explanation: Intrauterine insult or genetic abnormality is the most supported explanation. When weight, height, and head circumference all fall together, this pattern suggests a broader underlying problem affecting overall growth rather than isolated gastrointestinal loss.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because diarrhoea or malabsorption is more consistent with reduced weight gain without the same implication of all three measures falling together.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because structural or endocrine causes more typically affect weight and height, with head circumference usually relatively preserved.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because simultaneous downward crossing of weight, height, and head circumference is most suggestive of an intrauterine insult or genetic abnormality.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because constitutional growth delay does not usually explain head circumference also crossing down.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the pattern of all three parameters falling is clinically meaningful and helps narrow the aetiology.
